dave_acme: Hi team — our Private deployment (VPC vpc-0a1b2c) suddenly started failing when calling private.redwood.svc. We get DNS failures: `hostname not found` and 502s from the SDK. No infra changes on our side.
alice_support: Sorry you're hitting this, @dave_acme. Can you share the output of `dig +short private.redwood.svc` from one of your private instances and the `curl -v` error? Also which region and resolver setup (Route53 private hosted zones or outbound resolvers)?
dave_acme: Here you go, ran from an app pod:
```
$ dig +short private.redwood.svc

; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +short private.redwood.svc
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
And `curl -v https://private.redwood.svc/health` shows `Could not resolve host: private.redwood.svc`.
carmen_net: :eyes: That `no servers could be reached` usually means the VPC resolver rules aren't wired to the private hosted zone or an outbound resolver isn't reachable. Quick checks:
- Is there a Route53 private hosted zone for `redwood.svc`? If yes, is it associated with vpc-0a1b2c?
- Any overlapping private hosted zones in the account/other accounts with different records (split-horizon) that could cause ambiguous resolution?
dave_acme: We do have a PHZ created by the infra team a while ago, i see `redwood.svc (private)` in the console but Association shows 0 VPCs. Not sure how that happened.
ben_sre: That matches. Two possible causes we've seen:
1) PHZ lost association (manual removal or CloudFormation drift) -> returns NX/timeout for that VPC.
2) Resolver rule priority conflict (outbound resolver + conditional forwarding) where an outbound rule is hijacking lookup to public DNS.
ben_sre: Try these from an instance in the VPC and paste results:
```
# check resolver configuration
aws route53list-hosted-zones-by-name --dnsname "redwood.svc"
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z12345EXAMPLE
aws ec2 describe-vpcs --vpc-ids vpc-0a1b2c

# check resolver rules
aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules
aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0a1b2c
```
alice_support: Also can you `dig +trace private.redwood.svc` and `cat /etc/resolv.conf`? That helps confirm whether the instance's resolver points at the VPC resolver (AmazonProvidedDNS) or a custom DNS.
dave_acme: pastebin: https://paste.company/abc123 (dig/trace + resolv.conf). The trace shows queries going to the internet, not the VPC resolver; `resolv.conf` has `nameserver 10.0.0.2` (our VPC DNS) but the trace falls back.
carmen_net: If the trace goes to the internet, likely the PHZ association missing AND there's an outbound rule forwarding `redwood.svc` to another resolver (split-horizon). Also check for multiple PHZs with the same name across accounts — AWS will choose based on association order.
ben_sre: I've asked infra to re-associate the PHZ with vpc-0a1b2c and to check for duplicate PHZs. Temporary workaround: add a conditional forwarder on your VPC to our VPC resolver endpoint (if we give you one) or add entries to your hosts file for immediate testing.
devops-bot: [deploy] phz-association-change request created (#INC-4521) — assigned to infra-net.
ben_sre: Commands infra will run:
```
# re-associate PHZ
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z12345EXAMPLE --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c

# list duplicate zones
aws route53 list-hosted-zones | jq '.HostedZones[] | select(.Name=="redwood.svc.")'
```
dave_acme: Thanks — infra just confirmed they re-associated the PHZ and cleared a stale forwarding rule that had higher priority.
carmen_net: Can you confirm `dig +short private.redwood.svc` now?
dave_acme: Working now, returns `10.100.5.12`. SDK calls succeed. Thanks everyone :tada:
alice_support: Great — closing the loop. Root cause: PHZ lost association + stale outbound forwarding rule (split-horizon conflict). Action items: infra to add a CloudFormation guard to prevent PHZ drift and notify on association changes. I'll open a follow-up ticket for guards.
ben_sre: Recommended preventive steps we gave infra:
- Add CFN drift detection on PHZ stacks
- Tag PHZs and require cross-account checks before creating overlapping PHZs
- Monitor Route53 Resolver rule changes via CloudTrail + alert on rule priority edits
alice_support: Marking this resolved. If anything else pops up, reopen the thread or DM.
